throughout Seder Moed, wherever this pair appears, [some] replace R' Yochanan and insert R' Yonatan

and the cover was a handbreadth
the Ark nine and the cover a handbreadth: here are ten
and it is written 'I will meet with you there and speak with you from above the cover' (Ex 25:22) -- adduced as the source of the ten-handbreadth minimum
R' Yose: the Shekhina never descended below
R' Yose: and Moses and Elijah never ascended on high
R' Yose's verse: 'the heavens are the heavens of the Lord, and the earth He gave to the children of man' (Ps 115:16)
the stam's answer, twice: [the Shekhina's descent onto Sinai and onto the Mount of Olives was] above ten handbreadths
the stam's answer, three times: [Moses's and Elijah's ascent was] below ten
R' Tanchum on 'He grasps the face of the throne and spreads His cloud upon him' (Job 26:9): the Almighty spread of the radiance of His Shekhina and His cloud upon him
granted the Ark nine, as it is written '... and a cubit and a half its height' (Ex 25:10)
R' Chanina's teaching: for every vessel Moses made the Torah gave length, width and height; for the cover it gave length and width but not height
go and learn from the smallest of the vessels: 'and you shall make for it a frame of a handbreadth around' (Ex 25:25) -- as there a handbreadth, so here a handbreadth
if you grasped much you did not grasp; if you grasped little you grasped
the tzitz is like a gold plate, two fingers wide, stretching ear to ear, written on it in two lines: the Name above and 'kodesh l-' below
R' Eliezer b. R' Yose: I saw it in Rome, and 'holy to the Lord' was written on it in one line
one derives a vessel from a vessel, and does not derive a vessel from an ornament
as the master said: the crown is of any size
one derives a vessel from a vessel, and does not derive a vessel from a vessel's finish
its [the table's] frame was below
its frame was above
rather: one derives a thing whose measure the Torah gave from a thing whose measure the Torah gave; let the tzitz and the crown, for which the Torah gave no measure at all, not prove
Rav Huna: from here -- 'upon the face of the cover, eastward' (Lev 16:14)
and there is no face less than a handbreadth
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: Rav Huna learns 'face'-'face': here 'before (penei) the cover' (Lev 16:2), there 'from the presence (penei) of Isaac his father' (Gen 27:30)
Rav Acha bar Yaakov: we have it by tradition that the cherubs' faces are not less than a handbreadth
and Rav Huna too learns from here [the cherubs' faces, Ex 25:20]
what is a keruv? R' Abbahu: like a child (ke-ravya), for in Babylonia they call a child ravya
'the house King Solomon built ... thirty cubits its height' (I Kgs 6:2) and 'the height of the one cherub was ten cubits, and so the second' (I Kgs 6:26)
the baraita: as in the eternal House the cherubs stand at a third of the house, so in the Tabernacle the cherubs stand at a third of the house
the Tabernacle was ten cubits high: 'ten cubits the length of the board' (Ex 26:16)
sixty handbreadths; a third is twenty; take away the ten of the Ark and the cover, ten remain [from the cover to the cherubs' wings]
'and the cherubs shall spread their wings upward, screening (sokhekhim) the cover with their wings' (Ex 25:20)
the Merciful One called it 'sekhakh' above ten
R' Meir: all the cubits were middling
R' Yehuda: the cubit of building is six handbreadths, that of vessels five
rather, for R' Yehuda it [the ten handbreadths] is a received halakha
Rav: measures are halakha to Moses from Sinai
Rav: interpositions are halakha to Moses from Sinai
Rav: partitions are halakha to Moses from Sinai

wheat -- for the leprous house (the time of eating a half-loaf of wheat bread)

the mishnah: one who enters a leprous house with his clothes on his shoulders -- he and they impure at once; dressed -- he impure at once, they pure until he stays as long as eating a half-loaf, of wheat bread not barley, reclining and eating with relish
barley -- the barleycorn bone
the mishnah: a bone the size of a barleycorn imparts impurity by contact and carrying, not by tent
vine -- a revi'it of wine for the nazirite
fig -- a dried fig for carrying out on Shabbat
pomegranate -- householders' vessels, [whose measure is] as pomegranates
the mishnah: all householders' vessels -- their measure is as pomegranates
'a land of olive oil' -- a land all of whose measures are olives
rather say: most of its measures are olives
honey -- the large date for Yom Kippur
are measures written? rather they are halakhot, and the verse is a mere asmachta
'and he shall bathe his flesh in water' (Lev 14:9) -- that nothing interpose between him and the water
when the halakha came, it was for his hair
Rabba bar bar Chana: a single knotted hair interposes
three do not interpose
'et besaro' -- what is subordinate to his flesh, and what is that? his hair
when the halakha came, it was for R' Yitzchak's teaching
R' Yitzchak: by Torah law, [an interposition over] most of him that he is particular about interposes
and one he is not particular about does not interpose
and they decreed on most-of-him-not-particular because of most-of-him-particular
and on a-minority-he-is-particular-about because of most-of-him-particular

when the halakha came, it was for gud, lavud and the bent wall

objections.gloss_en: ואימא דמידלי טובא? -- say they were very high (presses Rav Acha's answer)

answered_by.gloss_en: מי כתיב למעלה למעלה?

objections.gloss_en: הניחא לרבי מאיר ... אלא לרבי יהודה ... ארון וכפורת כמה הוו להו? תמניא ופלגא, פשו להו חד סרי ופלגא -- אימא סוכה עד דהויא חד סרי ופלגא! (5b.11-12)

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא לרבי יהודה הלכתא גמירי לה (= p_yehuda_hilkheta): for R' Yehuda the reckoning is not the source

objections.gloss_en: שיעורין דאורייתא נינהו! דכתיב ארץ חטה ושעורה ..., ואמר רב חנין: כל הפסוק הזה לשיעורין נאמר; closed at 6a.8: אלמא דאורייתא נינהו!

answered_by.gloss_en: ותסברא? שיעורין מי כתיבי? אלא הלכתא נינהו וקרא אסמכתא בעלמא (= p_asmachta)

objections.gloss_en: כל שיעוריה סלקא דעתך?! הא איכא הני דאמרינן!

answered_by.gloss_en: אלא אימא: שרוב שיעוריה כזיתים (= p_rov_kezeitim)

objections.gloss_en: חציצין דאורייתא נינהו! דכתיב: ורחץ את בשרו במים -- שלא יהא דבר חוצץ בינו לבין המים

answered_by.gloss_en: כי אתאי הלכתא לשערו (= p_hlmm_searo) -- dropped after 6a.11
כי אתאי הלכתא לכדרבי יצחק (= p_hlmm_kidr_yitzchak) -- the answer the text ends with

objections.gloss_en: שערו נמי דאורייתא נינהו, דכתיב ורחץ את בשרו -- את הטפל לבשרו, ומאי ניהו? שערו! -- unanswered: the text moves to R' Yitzchak's teaching
וליגזר נמי על מיעוטו שאינו מקפיד משום מיעוטו המקפיד, אי נמי משום רובו שאינו מקפיד!

answered_by.gloss_en: היא גופא גזירה, ואנן ניקום ונגזר גזירה לגזירה?! (= p_gezera_ligzera)

objections.gloss_en: מחיצין -- הא דאמרן. הניחא לרבי יהודה, אלא לרבי מאיר מאי איכא למימר? -- for R' Meir the ten is derived from verses (5b.9-11)

answered_by.gloss_en: כי אתאי הלכתא -- לגוד, ולבוד, ודופן עקומה (= p_hlmm_gud_lavud, aliba R' Meir)
